About the role:
Aurizon Network Asset Management is looking for a motivated Civil / Structural Engineer to join our Civil and Structures Assets team and help shape the future of one of Australia’s most important rail networks.
You will contribute to the asset management strategy that connects inland producers with ports along the Queensland coast, from Bowen through Sarina to Gladstone. This is a broad, hands-on role offering exposure to the full asset lifecycle—from understanding asset condition and risk through to shaping renewal scopes, budgets, designs and delivery priorities.
You will help develop capital renewal and maintenance programs across a diverse civil and structures portfolio, including:
- Structures — more than 4,000 culverts, 300 bridges, retaining walls and other structural assets
- Level crossings — more than 700 crossings with a mix of active and passive controls
- Geotechnical and earthworks — steep slopes through several mountain ranges and the formation supporting the track asset
- Access points and access roads — connecting our teams safely and efficiently with railway infrastructure
- Corridor security and fencing — supporting a rail network across an area larger than Tasmania
Working closely with Design Management, Program Management, operations and maintenance teams, you will influence practical, whole-of-business outcomes from concept and design through to delivery of renewal works—balancing safety, risk, track access, cost and scope.
- Influence stakeholders across the business to achieve better outcomes for civil and structures assets
- Assess asset condition, defects and failure modes, applying risk-based engineering judgement to support investment decisions
- Develop renewal and maintenance scopes, budgets and forward programs, and manage changes through planning and delivery
- Improve the processes, tools and data used to make asset management decisions
- Develop and refine strategies, standards, policies and practical engineering guidelines
- Analyse asset information and translate it into clear priorities and recommendations
Around 20% of your time will be spent in the field travelling across the network, giving you direct exposure to the assets you manage and the people who operate and maintain them. The balance offers flexible working across the office and home.
About you:
You are an early-to-mid career Civil or Structural Engineer who is ready to broaden your experience beyond a single project or discipline. You bring experience in design, construction and/or asset management, and you are keen to apply your technical knowledge in a practical operational environment. You enjoy solving complex problems, learning from experienced professionals and working with a wide range of stakeholders to turn sound engineering into real-world outcomes.

- Bachelor of Civil Engineering or equivalent (mandatory)
- Approximately 2–8 years’ experience in a civil or structural engineering role (mandatory)

- A practical understanding of infrastructure operations, design, construction, maintenance and safety requirements
- Clear communication skills and the confidence to consult, negotiate and influence at different levels of the business
- The ability to apply legislation, regulation, standards and engineering requirements in a practical and proportionate way
- Strong written communication skills, with an interest in developing standards, specifications, policies, guidelines and processes
- Commercial awareness and the ability to balance risk, performance, cost and deliverability

At Aurizon, we support the development and growth of our employees. With a national portfolio of operations, we offer long-term and exciting career opportunities. 
Some of our benefits include:
- Development and growth opportunities.
- Access to mentoring and development programs.
- Discounts on selected health insurance funds, personal travel, gyms, vehicles and retail brands.

Aurizon is Australia’s largest rail freight operator and a top 100 ASX company. Each year, we deliver more than 250 million tonnes of Australian commodities right across the country. Aurizon is crucial to the Australian economy, connecting miners, primary producers and industry with international and domestic markets.

At Aurizon, we are proud of our diverse, collaborative, creative and high-performance culture. We celebrate the contribution of every employee and provide opportunities for career development in a dynamic, caring, and inclusive work environment.

·       Undertake and verify engineering calculations and technical assessments to develop, optimise and confirm the performance and constructability of civil works and associated building components.
·       Review architectural, structural and civil engineering drawings and specifications to assess constructability and engineering requirements, and provide technical input into quantity take-offs, cost estimates and budget control.
·       Assess proposed design changes and construction variations for their engineering, constructability, compliance, program and cost impacts, and prepare technical recommendations to support variation management.

- Assisting with quantity take-offs and pricing
- Preparing and issuing subcontractor and supplier enquiries
- Reviewing and comparing quotations
- Assisting with tender submissions
- Understanding project scope, methodology and construction requirements
- Building relationships with subcontractors and suppliers
- Working with our project delivery team to understand how estimates translate into live projects
- Developing your knowledge of commercial construction costs, trades and procurement
We don't expect you to know how to do all of this on day one. We'll teach you.
What we do expect is that you genuinely want to learn.
We're looking for someone who is curious, switched-on and interested in understanding how and why things are built and what they cost.

- Construction Management
- Quantity Surveying
- Civil Engineering
- Building & Construction
- Project Management
- Engineering

- Has strong numerical and analytical skills
- Has excellent attention to detail
- Can read information carefully and ask questions when something doesn't make sense
- Is organised and able to manage competing priorities
- Communicates confidently and professionally
- Takes ownership of their work
- Has a genuine interest in building a long-term career in commercial construction
WIP Construction is an established Cairns-based commercial construction company delivering projects throughout Cairns and Far North Queensland.
You'll be joining a team where you'll have the opportunity to learn from experienced construction professionals and gain exposure to real commercial projects from tender through to delivery.
This isn't a graduate role where you'll spend months watching from the sidelines.
You'll be given real work, real responsibility and plenty of support while you develop your skills.
For the right person, there is significant opportunity to grow within the business and develop into an experienced Estimator.
If you're motivated, good with numbers, interested in construction and looking for somewhere to start your career, we'd like to hear from you.
Apply through SEEK with your resume and a short cover letter telling us a little about yourself, what you're currently studying or have completed, and why estimating and commercial construction interests you.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is starting their career in drafting, estimating or construction and would like to develop practical skills within the steel fabrication and construction industry.
You will work closely with our experienced team and receive training and support to develop your knowledge of steel framing, estimating, drafting and construction processes.
Key Responsibilities
- Prepare and update technical drawings and construction documentation using CAD software
- Assist with preparing project estimates, including material quantities, labour and costs
- Read and interpret architectural and engineering drawings
- Assist with material takeoffs for steel framing and other construction materials
- Review project drawings, specifications and other documents to identify project requirements
- Work with project managers, engineers and other team members to obtain information required for drafting and estimating
- Maintain estimating information, project records and documentation
- Assist with site visits, measurements and inspections when required
- Prepare and update estimating templates and documentation
- Check drawings, quantities and estimates for accuracy and completeness
- Assist the team in identifying practical and cost-effective solutions
- Learn and develop knowledge of steel framing, construction methods, materials and estimating processes
What We're Looking For
- A qualification or relevant study in drafting, estimating, construction or a related field is preferred
- Basic to intermediate knowledge of CAD software, particularly AutoCAD or similar
- Good understanding of mathematics and attention to detail
- Ability to read and understand architectural and engineering drawings
- Good computer skills, including Microsoft Excel and Word
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- Organised and able to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines
- A willingness to learn and develop technical skills
- A practical and positive approach to problem-solving
- Construction, steel fabrication or manufacturing experience would be an advantage
- Previous experience with estimating software or project management systems would be an advantage, but is not essential
Full training will be provided for the right candidate.
We are happy to consider applicants who have recently completed their studies or have limited industry experience but demonstrate a strong willingness to learn.
What We Offer
At Dynamic Steelform, we are committed to providing a supportive and practical working environment where you can develop your skills and build a long-term career.
We offer:
- Competitive salary based on qualifications and experience
- On-the-job training and ongoing technical development
- The opportunity to gain practical experience in steel framing, drafting and estimating
- Training and support from experienced team members
- Opportunities for career progression as your skills develop
- A safe, friendly and respectful workplace
- A stable position within an established Western Australian company
- The opportunity to work with modern machinery, technology and construction systems
- A workplace that values teamwork, reliability and continuous improvement
About Dynamic Steelform
Dynamic Steelform is a Western Australian company specialising in steel fabrication and construction solutions.
Based in Forrestdale, we manufacture and supply steel framing and a range of steel building products for residential, commercial and construction projects.
Our business combines drafting, estimating, manufacturing and construction, giving our team members the opportunity to gain practical experience across different areas of the industry.
We are a growing and established business that values quality, reliability, teamwork and continuous improvement. We are committed to developing our people and providing opportunities for employees who want to build a long-term career in the construction and steel industry.
Apply Now
If you are interested in drafting, estimating or the construction industry and are looking for an opportunity to develop your skills, we would like to hear from you.
Please submit your resume and a short cover letter explaining your experience and why you are interested in the position.
Portfolio or examples of drafting work can also be provided if available.
We look forward to hearing from you and welcoming the right person to our team in Forrestdale.

bullets: Earn while you learn with a fulltime, paid Certificate III in Civil Construction
candidates.content_text:
Work Type: Maximum Term Full-Time - 36 Months
Location: Emerald
Directorate: Operations
Award & Salary: In accordance with relevant industrial agreements, including the applicable Award, Order or Certified Agreement.
Central Highlands Regional Council (CHRC) is seeking a reliable and motivated individual to join our Infrastructure section as a Civil Construction Trainee. This is an exciting opportunity to gain full-time, paid employment while completing a Certificate III in Civil Construction. 
As a trainee, you'll develop practical skills through a combination of on-the-job experience and formal training. Working alongside experienced crews, you'll gain valuable hands-on experience in the civil construction industry while building the skills, knowledge, and qualifications needed for a rewarding career in infrastructure and construction. 
 What you’ll bring 
 - A positive attitude and a genuine desire to learn 
 - A reliable approach to teamwork, with a focus on safety and following instructions 
 - An interest in working outdoors and developing practical civil construction skills 
 - A willingness to learn to safely operate a range of tools, equipment, and civil construction plant 
 - Commitment to completing a Certificate III in Civil Construction 
 - A current minimum Queensland C Class Provisional Driver’s Licence 
 - A General Construction Induction (White Card), or willingness to obtain one prior to commencement 
 What you'll be doing 
 - Assisting with the construction and maintenance of roads, drainage systems, and other civil infrastructure 
 - Learning to safely operate a range of hand tools, power tools, equipment, and civil construction plant 
 - Supporting excavation, earthworks, and site preparation activities 
 - Assisting with road repairs, gravel re-sheeting, pavement construction, and maintenance works 
 - Installing and maintaining drainage structures and stormwater infrastructure 
 - Undertaking traffic management and work site setup activities in accordance with safety requirements 
 - Carrying out labouring duties as part of a civil construction crew 
 Why work for Central Highlands Regional Council? 
At CHRC, we're committed to creating opportunities for the next generation of skilled workers. As the winner of the 2022 and 2024 Regional Queensland Training Awards – Large Employer of the Year, as well as producing the 2022 Apprentice of the Year and 2023 Equity Student of the Year, we have a proven track record of supporting apprentices and trainees to achieve their career goals. 
No matter where you want your career to take you, CHRC can help you get there. At CHRC, there’s a rewarding path and an incredible future waiting for you. Through hands-on experience, structured training, and supportive mentoring, you'll have the opportunity to develop valuable skills, gain a nationally recognised qualification, and build a rewarding career close to home. 
We also offer great benefits, including: 
 - A generous superannuation scheme 
 - Five weeks annual leave with 17.5% leave loading 
 - Fortnightly RDO’s 
 - Full uniform allocation 
 - Payroll deductions and salary sacrifice options 
 - Wages paid fortnightly 
 - Employee Assistance Program 
 - Fitness Passport member benefits 
 To be eligible for this traineeship, you must: 
 - Be at least 17 years of age and no longer at school 
 - Meet citizen, residency, and visa requirements to undertake a traineeship 
 - Not hold a qualification equal to or higher than the traineeship qualification in the same field 
 Where trainee positions are funded through government initiatives, they may be subject to additional eligibility requirements. We strongly encourage applications from the following groups: 
 - Young people (aged 15–24 years, including those in and transitioned from out-of-home care) 
 - Long-term unemployed job seekers 
 - Mature-age job seekers (aged 45 years or older) 
 - Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people 
 - Migrants and refugees 
 - People with disability 
 - Displaced workers 
 - Women re-entering the workforce 
 - Veterans and ex-service personnel and their families 
 How to apply: 
Please download and review the position description. (linked) 
To apply, submit the following documents: 
 - Your resume detailing relevant experience or work history 
 Although it’s not mandatory, you may also submit a cover letter outlining your skills and motivation for applying if you wish. 
Applicants selected to progress will be invited to participate in a shortlisting process. 
Pre-employment checks: 
Pre-employment checks for this role include: 
 - Right to Work in Australia 
 - Medical Assessment 
 - Reference Checks 
 - Licence Checks (if applicable) 
 - Funding Eligibility Checks 
 Whoever you are, there’s a place for you here. 
For a confidential discussion, please contact the Recruitment Team on 1300 242 686 during business hours.
Register your interest by submitting your resume.
Applications close: Monday 19th October 2026 at 8am.

candidates.abstract: An exciting opportunity to develop your career delivering civil construction projects across South East Queensland.
bullets: Work across civil projects valued between $5M and $80M
Join a team focused on safety, professional growth and wellbeing

candidates.content_text:
Take an active role in delivering civil construction projects across South East Queensland, with exposure to a range of project types and stages of construction.
Working closely with the Project Manager, Supervisors and site teams, you'll help coordinate site activities, monitor construction progress and ensure works meet programme, quality and safety requirements. This role offers hands-on involvement in project delivery, with opportunities to strengthen your technical skills and develop your construction experience.
Description
- Coordinate site activities, including daily inspections, subcontractors, plant and resources.
- Assist with construction planning, programming and monitoring progress against project schedules.
- Manage project documentation, quality assurance records and progress reporting.
- Track costs, quantities and resource requirements, escalating issues where required.
- Work with Project Managers and site teams to resolve technical and construction-related issues.
- Ensure works comply with project specifications, contractual obligations and safety requirements.
Profile
- Previous experience as a Site Engineer within civil construction.
- Exposure to subdivisions, earthworks, drainage, roads or other civil construction works.
- An understanding of construction drawings, specifications, quality assurance and project documentation.
- Strong communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with site teams and subcontractors.
- Civil Engineering qualification.
Job Offer
- Long-term opportunities with an established civil contractor
- Support from experienced Project Managers and construction teams
- Local SEQ projects, with the benefit of being home each night
- Employee wellness initiatives and support
- A collaborative team with opportunities to grow
About Brunel:
Brunel is a recruitment and flexible workforce solution provider which connects talented people with opportunities throughout Australasia and around the world. We specialise in highly skilled roles across a variety of technical, professional, trades and craft disciplines, pairing candidates with industry-leading projects and organisations on a contract, permanent or secondment basis.
Operating in Australasia since 1997, Brunel has major bases of operation in Perth, Sydney, Brisbane, Melbourne and Port Moresby, which are further backed by the strength and reach of a truly global network spanning over 45 countries, 120 offices and 50 years of successful operation.
Brunel is proud to be equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander and female candidates.
Do you have questions?
If you have any questions or would like to discuss the details of this role, please contact Laine on 0413 630 160 or l.thornton@brunel.net
